summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after multiple episodes of syncope. She reported a long history of falls, sometimes due to leg weakness and other times with sudden loss of awareness. In the emergency department, she had paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia with heart rates in the 170s, associated with hypotension and loss of consciousness. Her platelet count was critically low at 10,000, attributed to underlying immune thrombocytopenic purpura, possibly exacerbated by recent antibiotics and illness. She received two doses of IV immunoglobulin, with platelet count improving to 64,000. Her metoprolol was increased to 50 mg daily to control arrhythmia risk, and aspirin was held during admission but restarted at discharge. Valsartan was held due to stable blood pressure. She had no further syncopal or arrhythmic events during hospitalization. She was discharged home with a heart event monitor, follow-up planned with cardiology and hematology, and instructions to monitor weight and symptoms.
